account:
It is day 1, shortly after nine. I have read the office books and attended the morning office business. My next appointment is the mill grain inspection at ten. The builder delivered his signed visual bridge report and has explicitly confirmed receiving the agreed two emeralds. He found the crossing passable, but did not certify its structural safety or recommend a specific repair. No further work is authorized.

The unusual news is still vague: Townsfolk 28 and Townsfolk 08 have spoken of a 'bridge or port change' at the bakery. Townsfolk 28 also said the baker was there and had carried a sack of bread at the inn and plaza_north_1. I have not witnessed that change or established what those words describe. The report of a sack suggests a substantial bread delivery, but does not itself establish anything improper.

The baker came to the town hall asking whether meals or gatherings required bread. The secretary placed no order, and I have said no town hall meals are planned. The secretary says the innkeeper announced bread service yesterday evening, while guest rooms are not yet furnished. The innkeeper's written request was for advance notice of visitors or gatherings to avoid wasting food. These facts could fit an ordinary effort to supply or promote food service at the inn. They could also relate to some gathering or riverside arrangement I have not yet heard about, but that remains speculation.

The secretary reports no new correspondence or other verified news requiring action, and says the office books were secure. I have no evidence that the secretary, baker, innkeeper, or builder is concealing anything. I want to clarify exactly what changed at the bakery, who observed it, and its purpose, without treating a vague report as proof. I should preserve my ten o'clock mill appointment while following up.
